notes: CLARIFICATION — Two things named 'TurnCoordinator' must not be conflated: (1) **Formal Layer-2 TurnCoordinator component** — zero implementation, class TurnCoordinator does not exist (per CORE_COMPLETION_AUDIT_20260810.md §8, line 113; zero implementation is a non-blocking architectural gap). De-facto handled by router.py::route_request() + lead_candidate_handler.py. (2) **TC2-TC10 distributed functional machinery** — MERGED (PRs #562–#588, 08–10/08/2026), WIRED (4 unconditional callback sites in app.py for TC8 turn-state r/w), VERIFIED in staging (TC10_OPERATIONAL_VERIFICATION_HARNESS.md, verify_tc8/9_staging.py runs PASS, regression matrix 21/21 stable). This node's code_paths register the machinery; its status="shadow" and precedence="frozen decision contract planning-only" refer to formal Layer-2 authority (not yet approved), not machinery implementation status.

BUG_AUDIT_LOG.md added as a canonical doc 2026-07-28 (N17 pilot Task 3 fix): BUG-130 (line 3056, create-vs-update misroute in core/lead_candidate_handler.py) and BUG-140 (line 3198, unrelated-lead overwrite risk, still pending) are both registered, unfixed, and 142 lines apart in the same log section — the pilot's Librarian-track investigation grepped BUG-130 and never read far enough to find BUG-140. See task_profiles/profiles.json's `turn_coordinator_routing.bounded_local_expansions`, which now inlines both entries into the bundle so this cannot be missed by stopping at the first match.

TC7 status note: TC7-B1 claim authorization (core/claim_authorization.py, PR #583/#587) is built but has zero live consumers — grep confirms zero references outside its own test file. TC7-B2 dual-signal shadow comparison (PR #591, ClaimAuthorizationShadow) deployed but produced zero observed log output in CORE_COMPLETION_AUDIT verification (no caller of TC7-B2's log marker found in retained windows). RP5 evidence finalization is shadow-stage (FEATURE_EVIDENCE_FINALIZER=shadow on both Prod/Staging per live env-var confirmation); enforcement not enabled.
route_request and handle_lead_candidate are current de-facto routing/ownership surfaces; TC2-TC10 machinery now standardizes these through typed contracts (ownership_contracts.py).
The coordinator consumes typed signals and must not invent business state or approval policy.

PR #471 changed who legitimately owns a turn's final reply, not just how routing is observed: when FEATURE_SINGLE_SPEAKER_APPROVAL_UX is on and this turn queued an approval, run_agent() hands the reply to the Gateway (reply_owner="gateway") and returns immediately without a further Agent turn (app.py:3802 as of ffa678a7; line drifts with unrelated wording-only edits elsewhere in the file, e.g. PR #479/#480 — re-verified this audit that the boundary logic itself is unchanged). This is a conditional, code-level ownership assignment for approval-queuing turns specifically — it does not create a general reply_owner claim mechanism and does not resolve the concurrency race (a callback and a concurrent text turn for the same identity) described in docs/architecture/turn-coordinator/REPLY_OWNERSHIP_AND_APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_RESEARCH.md §1.3c, which remains unmitigated and research-only.

The same handoff path still invokes the RP5 shadow observer (observe_shadow_finalizer, app.py:3813 as of ffa678a7) on the Gateway-owned reply before returning — RP5's classification runs even though the Agent's own LLM text is never produced for that turn; see layer.rp5's notes.

PR2 (merged 2026-07-29) added an early, anchored approval-lifecycle resolver ahead of lead capture, Session, Router, Business Memory, and Agent — a specialized deterministic bypass, not a replacement for formal TurnCoordinator. Unrecognized text falls through to the existing route; both paths remain live.
